about: EchoStar is a US satellite and wireless company based in Englewood, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (SATS). Its Hughes unit sells HughesNet satellite internet and network equipment for consumers, enterprises and governments. It merged with Dish Network in December 2023, adding Boost Mobile, Sling TV and a 5G network build, and in 2025 agreed to sell spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX. Founded by Charlie Ergen, it has revenue of around $15 billion. Boost Mobile and Sling are recognised US consumer brands.

wiki.title: EchoStar
wiki.text: EchoStar Corporation is an American telecommunications company, specializing in satellite communication, wireless telecommunications, and internet services. Echostar also provides multichannel video programming and mobile services through its subsidiaries: Dish Network, Boost Mobile, Sling TV, EchoStar Mobile, and Hughes Network Systems.

about: Hainan Airlines is a Chinese full-service airline founded in 1993 and based on Hainan island, a subsidiary of HNA group, now flagship of Hainan Airlines Holding under a 2021 restructuring led by Liaoning Fangda. Flies domestic and international routes from Haikou, Beijing and elsewhere, serving leisure and business travellers. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600221). Well-known Chinese carrier with a Skytrax five-star rating history.

wiki.title: Hainan Airlines
wiki.text: Hainan Airlines is an airline headquartered in Haikou, Hainan, China. It is the largest civilian-run Chinese air transport company, making it the fourth-largest airline in terms of fleet size in the People's Republic of China, and the tenth-largest airline in Asia in terms of passengers carried. It operates scheduled domestic and international services on 500 routes from Hainan and various locations on the mainland, as well as charter services. Its main base is located at Haikou Meilan International Airport, with hubs at Beijing-Capital, Chongqing, Shenzhen and Xi'an, along with several focus cities.

about: American Airlines is the world's largest airline by fleet size and passengers, flying to over 350 destinations from hubs in Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte, Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia and Phoenix, and a member of Oneworld. Revenue near 54 billion dollars, with about 130,000 employees. Headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas; formed 1930. Listed on Nasdaq (AAL). Has restructured after the 2013 US Airways merger. Household US consumer brand with long-standing sports naming rights (American Airlines Center and Arena).

wiki.title: American Airlines
wiki.text: American Airlines, Inc. is a major airline in the United States headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, within the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex. It is the largest airline in the world in terms of passengers carried and daily flights. American, along with its regional subsidiaries and contractors operating under the brand name American Eagle, operates an extensive international and domestic network with almost 6,800 flights per day to nearly 350 destinations in 48 countries. The airline is also a founding member of Oneworld alliance, one of the world's three major airline alliances.

about: United Airlines is one of the largest US carriers, flying passengers and cargo to more than 300 destinations from hubs in Chicago, Newark, Houston, Denver, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Washington, as a Star Alliance member with the MileagePlus loyalty programme. Revenue near 57 billion dollars and about 100,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago; part of United Airlines Holdings, listed on Nasdaq (UAL). Major US consumer brand with extensive sports and entertainment sponsorships.

wiki.title: United Airlines
wiki.text: United Airlines, Inc. is a major airline in the United States headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It operates an extensive domestic and international route network across the United States and to destinations on six continents. Regional service is provided by independent carriers operating under the United Express brand, and the Star Alliance, of which United was one of the five founding airlines, extends its network throughout the world.

about: Sumisho Air Lease is an aircraft leasing company, a subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Corporation, with a US office in Los Angeles. It buys commercial aircraft and engines and leases them to airlines, earning rental income and sale gains, and was later merged into the Sumitomo group aviation leasing platform. Funding of about $19bn in the input appears to be a debt or facility figure and may be garbled by OCR. B2B lessor with no consumer profile, and a poor sponsorship target.

about: LATAM Airlines Group is Latin America's largest airline group, headquartered in Santiago, Chile, with affiliates in Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador and Argentina, flying to over 140 destinations plus a cargo arm. It carries over 70 million passengers a year, with annual revenue near $13bn, and emerged from US Chapter 11 in 2022. Listed on the Santiago stock exchange (LTM) and NYSE ADRs. Strong regional consumer brand with sponsorship in sports across Latin America and international football.

wiki.title: LATAM Airlines
wiki.text: LATAM Airlines is a Chilean multinational airline headquartered in Santiago, Chile. It is the largest airline holding company in Latin America with subsidiaries in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay and Peru.

about: Heathrow Airport Holdings owns and operates London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport and one of the world's largest hubs, handling about 83 million passengers a year across four terminals. It earns aeronautical charges from airlines and retail, parking and property revenue. Owned by a consortium led by Ferrovial, Qatar Investment Authority, Canada's CDPQ and GIC, Alinda, USS and others, with Ferrovial reducing its stake. Private. Hugely recognised consumer-facing brand, with premium sponsorship opportunities.

wiki.title: Heathrow Airport Holdings
wiki.what: Company based in the United Kingdom
wiki.text: Heathrow Airport Holdings is a company that operates and manages Heathrow Airport based in London, England. It was formed by the privatisation of the British Airports Authority as BAA plc as part of Margaret Thatcher's privatisation of government-owned assets, and was once a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

about: Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) operates Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, India's third busiest airport, handling over 40 million passengers a year, with a new Terminal 2. It earns airline charges, retail, advertising and property income. Owned by the GVK Group's successor Fairfax, Fairfax India Holdings (about 64 percent), with Siemens-related and Karnataka government stakes. Private. Consumer-facing airport brand in a major city, with sponsorship and advertising inventory.

gategroup is a Swiss airline catering and onboard services company, based in Glattbrugg near Zurich, supplying meals, retail products, equipment and lounges to airlines worldwide through more than 190 units in about 60 countries. It was acquired by RRJ Capital in 2016 and later had HNA and Temasek links, restructured and sold to new owners. Private. B2B with little consumer brand recognition, though its products are used on airlines passengers' flights.

wiki.title: Gategroup
wiki.what: Swiss company providing food-related services to the travel industry
wiki.text: Gategroup is a Swiss company providing services to the travel industry, including catering, onboard retail, food service provisioning, and food logistics. Gategroup operates more than 200 facilities in over 60 countries. Its head office is in Glattbrugg, Switzerland, near Zurich Airport.

about: Gol Linhas Aereas (Gol Transportes Aereos) is a Brazilian low-cost airline based in Sao Paulo, flying a Boeing 737 fleet on domestic and South American routes, with more than 30 million passengers a year. It filed for US Chapter 11 in January 2024 and emerged in June 2025 with Abra Group as its parent, after which it delisted from the NYSE and B3. Revenue is near BRL 20bn. Well-known Brazilian consumer airline brand, with football and sports sponsorship history.

wiki.title: Gol Linhas Aéreas
wiki.text: GOL Linhas Aéreas S.A is a Brazilian low cost airline based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. According to the National Civil Aviation Agency of Brazil (ANAC), between January and December 2019, GOL had 37.7% of the domestic and 3.8% of the international market shares in terms of passenger-kilometers flown, making it the largest domestic and third largest international airline in Brazil.

about: Virgin Atlantic Airways is a British long-haul airline based in Crawley, West Sussex, flying from London Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester to North America, the Caribbean, Africa, India and Asia, with about 40 aircraft and over 5 million passengers a year. Delta Air Lines holds 49 percent, Virgin Group 51 percent, and the airline is private. It emerged from a 2020 rescue package. Strong consumer brand with the Virgin name, and sponsorship and brand tie-ins.

wiki.title: Virgin Atlantic
wiki.text: Virgin Atlantic, a trading name of Virgin Atlantic Airways Limited and Virgin Atlantic International Limited, is a British airline with its head office in Crawley, West Sussex, England. The airline was established in 1984 as British Atlantic Airways, and was originally planned by its co-founders Randolph Fields and Alan Hellary to fly between London and the Falkland Islands. Soon after changing the name to Virgin Atlantic Airways, Fields sold his shares in the company to Richard Branson in return for unlimited free travel. Its maiden flight from London–Gatwick to Newark took place on 22 June 1984.

about: Grupo Aeromexico is Mexico's flag-carrier airline group based in Mexico City, flying domestic and international routes to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia from its Mexico City hub, and a founding member of the SkyTeam alliance. It carries about 25 million passengers a year, with a fleet of roughly 150 aircraft. Delta Air Lines owns a stake of around 20 percent. It returned to the Mexican exchange and the NYSE in 2025 (AEROMEX). High consumer brand awareness in Mexico.

wiki.title: Grupo Aeroméxico
wiki.text: Grupo Aeroméxico S.A.B. de C.V. is an airline holding company headquartered in Mexico City. Grupo Aeroméxico owns and operates Aeroméxico, the principal airline of Mexico.

about: Spirit Airlines is a US ultra-low-cost carrier, historically headquartered in Miramar, Florida and now shown near Dania Beach, with a fleet of Airbus A320 family aircraft flying across the US, Caribbean and Latin America under a bare-fare, pay-for-extras model. It failed to merge with Frontier or JetBlue, filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2024 and again in 2025, and has been shrinking. Founded 1983. Recognisable consumer brand, but financially distressed, so a weak sponsorship prospect.

Shanghai-based flag carrier airline, one of China's big three, flying domestic and international routes, member of SkyTeam, state-owned and listed in Shanghai, Hong Kong and NYSE. Revenue about CNY 140 billion. Strong consumer brand in China. Part of China Eastern Air Holdings, with a fleet of over 700 aircraft. Hub airports in Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao. Strong consumer brand across China.

wiki.title: China Eastern Airlines
wiki.text: China Eastern Airlines is a major airline in China, headquartered in Minhang, Shanghai. It is one of the three major airlines in the country, along with Air China and China Southern Airlines.

about: HALO AirFinance is a joint venture between Tokyo Century and Carlyle Aviation Partners, based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, formed to provide aircraft finance, specifically financing for commercial airlines and lessors. Customers are airlines and aircraft owners. Funding of about 390 million dollars is shown. B2B financial services business with no consumer brand awareness, though both parents are well known in finance and aviation.

about: Virgin Australia is Australia's second-largest airline, headquartered in Brisbane, flying domestic and some international routes with a leisure and business offer and the Velocity Frequent Flyer programme. It entered administration in 2020 and was bought by US private equity firm Bain Capital, relaunching as a mid-market carrier. Bain Capital reintroduced it to the ASX in 2025, with Qatar Airways taking a minority stake. Revenue is over 5 billion Australian dollars. High consumer awareness in Australia, and has sponsored motorsport and other sport in the past.

Willis Mitsui & Co. Engine Support is a Dublin-based aircraft engine leasing joint venture between Willis Lease Finance and Mitsui & Co., providing aircraft engines to airlines worldwide on lease. Recorded funding is about $750 million. Customers are airlines and maintenance firms. B2B with low public brand awareness.

Malaysian low-cost airline brand founded in 2001 by Tony Fernandes, now under the Capital A group, flying across Asia with about 200 aircraft. Large following, sponsor of football and motorsport. Tony Fernandes and Kamarudin Meranun bought the airline in 2001 for a token sum. Fernandes also ran the Caterham Formula 1 team and the airline sponsored F1 outfits in that period. The AirAsia group, now Capital A, also has the AirAsia Move super-app. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia.

wiki.title: AirAsia
wiki.text: AirAsia Group Berhad, operating as AirAsia, is a Malaysian multinational low-cost airline headquartered near Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Established in 1993 and commencing operations in 1996, the airline is the largest in Malaysia by fleet size and destinations. It operates scheduled domestic and international flights to over 166 destinations across 25 countries. Its primary hub is Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), where it operates from Terminal 2, the low-cost carrier terminal.

about: Sichuan Airlines is a Chinese airline based in Chengdu, operating an all-Airbus fleet of more than 150 aircraft on domestic and international routes, with Chengdu Tianfu and Shuangliu airports as key hubs. It was founded in 1986 and its shareholders include Sichuan Airlines Group, Shandong Airlines Group and other state-linked entities. It is known for its Tibetan routes and for the 2018 cockpit window incident. It is a well known Chinese consumer airline brand, with annual passenger numbers in the tens of millions.

China Southern Airlines is one of China's three largest state-owned airlines, headquartered in Guangzhou, with a fleet of around 900 aircraft serving more than 200 destinations. It flies from hubs in Guangzhou and Beijing Daxing, and is a member of the SkyTeam alliance. Revenue is above 20 billion dollars and it carries more than 100 million passengers a year. Controlled by China Southern Air Holding, a state-owned enterprise, and listed in Shanghai (600029), Hong Kong (1055) and NYSE (ZNH). Strong consumer brand in China and Asia.

wiki.title: China Southern Airlines
wiki.text: China Southern Airlines is a major airline in China, headquartered in Guangzhou, Guangdong. It is one of the three major airlines in the country, along with Air China and China Eastern Airlines.

about: Car rental company operating Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands at airports and city locations in North America, Europe and elsewhere, and renting to leisure and business travellers plus Firefly, and it has used EVs including Tesla in its fleet. Revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Estero, Florida; founded 1918. Listed on Nasdaq (HTZ), emerged from 2021 bankruptcy with Knighthead and Certares as large holders. Major consumer travel brand with a long motorsport and sports marketing record.

wiki.title: Hertz
wiki.text: The hertz is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event per second. The hertz is an SI derived unit whose formal expression in terms of SI base units is 1/s or s−1, meaning that one hertz is one per second or the reciprocal of one second. It is used only in the case of periodic events. It is named after Heinrich Rudolf Hertz (1857–1894), the first person to provide conclusive proof of the existence of electromagnetic waves. For high frequencies, the unit is commonly expressed in multiples: kilohertz (kHz), megahertz (MHz), gigahertz (GHz), terahertz (THz).

wiki.title: Hertz Global Holdings
wiki.text: Hertz Global Holdings, Inc., is an American car rental company based in Estero, Florida. The company operates its namesake Hertz brand, along with the brands Dollar Rent A Car, Firefly Car Rental, and Thrifty Car Rental.

about: Timeshare and vacation ownership company selling points-based membership at resorts under Hilton Grand Vacations, Diamond Resorts and Bluegreen, operating more than 150 properties in the US, Europe, Asia and the Caribbean, with about 700,000 owner families. Earns from sales, financing and management fees, with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun off from Hilton in 2017. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HGV). Consumer brand tied to Hilton.

Marriott Vacations Worldwide is a US timeshare and vacation ownership company that sells and manages vacation club points under Marriott Vacation Club, Westin, Sheraton, Hyatt and Interval International. Customers are vacation owners and members, with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun off from Marriott International in 2011. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (VAC). Consumer brands are licensed from Marriott.

Another Star is based in Leiden, the Netherlands, and is described by Crunchbase as a hotel chain that operates hotels and related hospitality and leisure businesses. The input lists hospitality, hotel and leisure as its industries and shows funding of about $2.0bn, with the latest round in November 2025. The business model is likely accommodation revenue, but the input gives no further detail on brands, size or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Brex is a San Francisco fintech providing corporate cards, spend management, expense software, travel and banking tools for start-ups and large businesses. Customers range from early-stage tech firms to large enterprises, and it earns interchange fees, software subscriptions and interest. Founded in 2017 by Henrique Dubugras and Pedro Franceschi, it raised over $1.6bn and was valued at about $12bn in 2022. Private. B2B brand known in tech and start-up circles.

F1 Arcade is an experiential hospitality venue brand that merges competitive racing simulators, bar and food in a social setting, with venues in London, Boston, Manchester, Birmingham and other cities, plus international expansion. Customers are consumers and corporate groups paying for simulator sessions, drinks and food. Founded in 2021 by Patrick Crooke, it uses Formula 1-style racing simulation. Funding shown is about 131 million. It is directly connected to motorsport, with high relevance for F1 audiences.
